scope: Proposition 9.13 (The instanton link and its phase degree) of the manuscript “Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere” (preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 306 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ee916c92b825a868), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 125-126. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Put n∗ = ntot D > 0 and η = n∗ − 1. At each legitimate cut-down instanton, the normal spinor link before phase quotient is S2n∗−1/{±1} and its phase quotient is CPn∗−1 . The phase-character-two line restricts to O(2) on this projective space. The η phase sections can be chosen so that their cut-down link is regular and has signed 125 count 2η sign(a). (9.12) There is one fixed overall boundary-orientation convention in this formula, the same for every instanton. Subsequent mixed branch terms may be kept zero near these links.
